cross_seed_matching.denominator_definition: the complete 121-candidate cohort frozen in Phase 1 -- every candidate is matched against the FULL target dictionary for both seed 1 and seed 2
cross_seed_matching.note_on_67: 67 is seed 2's reproduced_strong count, OUT OF THE FULL 121-candidate cohort (67/121, not out of any smaller eligible subset). It is not a denominator itself -- it is one cell of the seed_2 row, which sums to 121 across all six classifications.
cross_seed_matching.insufficient_evidence_identity_check: the same 25 feature_idx values are classified insufficient_evidence under BOTH seed_1 and seed_2 -- insufficiency is a property of the candidate's own Confirmation-subset firing volume (<5 tokens or <3 prompts), independent of which target seed it is matched against, so it is identical across both matching attempts. Verified programmatically: the two 25-element sets are equal.
cross_seed_matching.double_counting_check: each of the 121 candidates receives exactly one classification per seed (6 mutually exclusive categories); no candidate appears in more than one cell per seed.

cross_capacity_matching.denominator_definition: NOT the full 121-candidate cohort. Restricted, per the approved Phase 3 plan, to candidates whose PRIMARY REVIEW reached >= medium confidence (61 of the 121 candidates qualify: 26 high + 35 medium). This is a materially different, smaller, and differently-defined population than the cross-seed matching's 121-candidate denominator.
cross_capacity_matching.why_zero_insufficient_evidence_here: the >=medium-confidence filter already excludes every candidate that would have hit the minimum-evidence floor (confidence assignment during review already penalized/flagged thin Confirmation evidence) -- so by construction none of these 61 fall below the <5-token/<3-prompt threshold again here. This is a consequence of the confidence-based filter, not a separate finding.
cross_capacity_matching.explicit_warning: cross-capacity's 61-candidate denominator and cross-seed's 121-candidate denominator must never be combined, averaged, or compared cell-for-cell as if they were the same population. The superficial numeric closeness of cross-seed seed_2's reproduced_strong count (67, out of 121) and cross-capacity's eligible-candidate count (61, out of 121) is coincidental and was a source of confusion in the Phase 3 report -- corrected here.

full_121_accounting.method: every one of the 121 candidates is accounted for in BOTH the cross-seed table (which covers all 121) and, separately, in a binary medium+/below-medium split that determines cross-capacity eligibility (61 eligible, 60 not eligible for the cross-capacity check specifically, but still fully classified in cross-seed).
full_121_accounting.below_medium_confidence_definition: 121 total - 61 (>=medium) = 60 candidates at low or unvalidated confidence, NOT cross-capacity-checked, but fully present and classified in the cross-seed 121-row tables above.
